title: 3rd Stopping Place 4th Truth The Seal Of Unity In The Manifestation Of The Compassionate And The Provider

questions.question: What is the main point made through the example of a single apple?
questions.answer: Even one fruit shows that its giving and making depends on the One who controls the larger order of the world.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect an apple with the changing of seasons and the movement of day and night?
questions.answer: It shows that the fruit is tied to a wide system in nature, so its source cannot be limited to a small, separate cause.

questions.question: What image is used for the earth, and what does that image suggest?
questions.answer: The earth is compared to a ship carrying goods, which suggests that it is arranged to bring needed provisions to living beings.

questions.question: What do the marks found on the apple point to?
questions.answer: They point to purposeful making, wisdom, mercy, and dependence on the Creator.

questions.question: How does the passage move from one apple to all fruits, plants, and animals?
questions.answer: It says the same signs seen on one apple appear across all of them, so they come from the same Maker.

questions.question: Why is the maker of the apple also presented as the maker of the world’s creatures?
questions.answer: Because the apple belongs within the same ordered system as the other beings of the world and shares the same signs of creation.

questions.question: What is meant by calling the world the apple’s garden?
questions.answer: It means the apple grows within a much larger place prepared and managed for life and growth.

questions.question: What is meant by calling the universe the apple’s tree and the seasons its workshop?
questions.answer: It means the fruit is produced through a vast process that includes the whole created order and the cycles of time.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Divine unity through every fruit?
questions.answer: Each fruit acts like a sign that points to one Creator who made both that fruit and the whole universe.

questions.question: How does the final sentence strengthen the argument from one fruit?
questions.answer: It says every fruit repeats the same testimony, so the proof of Divine oneness is many times over.

questions.question: Which is the better summary of the passage: “Nature works by itself,” or “Creation shows one Lord over all”?
questions.answer: Creation shows one Lord over all.

questions.question: According to the passage, why can the giving of one apple not be explained by a small local cause alone?
questions.answer: Because producing and delivering it depends on the working of the whole world order.

questions.question: What larger realities are mentioned to show the scale behind one fruit?
questions.answer: The turning of seasons, the alternation of night and day, and the movement of the earth are mentioned.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the design seen on the apple’s surface?
questions.answer: It suggests that the apple carries clear signs of deliberate and wise creation.

questions.question: Name two qualities shown by the apple according to the passage.
questions.answer: Wisdom and mercy.

questions.question: What is the significance of saying the same signs appear on all apples and other living things?
questions.answer: It means they all come from one source rather than many unrelated makers.

questions.question: Why would many separate makers not fit the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: Because the same pattern and meaning appear everywhere in creation, pointing to one ruling will.

questions.question: What relationship is described between the apple and the rest of creation?
questions.answer: The apple is presented as connected with other creatures as part of one shared world and one system.

questions.question: In this passage, what role do spring and summer play?
questions.answer: They are described as the period in which the fruit develops and reaches completion.

questions.question: What does it mean that each fruit is a seal of unity?
questions.answer: Each fruit serves as a sign confirming that all creation belongs to one Creator.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the earth and the universe to writing?
questions.answer: It presents them like works that reveal their author through the signs found in every fruit.

questions.question: What overall conclusion should a reader draw from the passage?
questions.answer: Small created things can lead a person to recognize Allah’s oneness and lordship over all.

questions.question: What does the passage say is required for a person to receive even one apple as provision?
questions.answer: It requires the action of the One who governs the world’s movements and seasons.

questions.question: Why is the revolving earth mentioned in a discussion about fruit?
questions.answer: Because the fruit reaches people through a world arranged and moved in an ordered way.

questions.question: What does the comparison to a cargo ship add to the meaning?
questions.answer: It highlights that the earth carries and delivers provisions to those who need them.

questions.question: What kind of evidence does the apple provide in the passage?
questions.answer: It provides evidence of intentional creation and Divine care.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention not only apples but also fruits, plants, and animals?
questions.answer: To widen the proof from one example to the whole living world.

questions.question: How does the passage argue from similarity?
questions.answer: It says the same meaningful signs found in one apple are found in other created things too.

questions.question: What does calling the Creator the true owner and maker of the apple imply?
questions.answer: It implies that no lesser cause has independent control over the fruit’s existence and provision.

questions.question: How does the passage present the earth, the cosmos, and the seasons in relation to the apple?
questions.answer: They are presented as the larger environment and process through which the apple is produced.

questions.question: What idea is emphasized by describing every fruit as a seal?
questions.answer: That each fruit bears a repeated mark of the same Divine oneness.

questions.question: How do many fruits strengthen the witness to unity?
questions.answer: Each one adds another confirming sign, making the testimony widespread and strong.

questions.question: What is the central lesson for faith from this passage?
questions.answer: Reflecting on even a simple fruit can guide a person to recognize Allah’s power, wisdom, and unity.

questions.question: What claim does the passage make about the source of one apple given as sustenance?
questions.answer: Its source is the One who controls the whole order of the world.

questions.question: Why are the cycles of time mentioned alongside the apple?
questions.answer: Because the fruit depends on those cycles for its coming into being and reaching people.

questions.question: How is the earth’s movement described, and why is that description meaningful?
questions.answer: It is pictured as a vessel carrying goods, showing that provision is transported through a planned system.

questions.question: What does the passage communicate by saying people stand waiting for fruits?
questions.answer: It shows their need and their dependence on provision sent to them.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from finding those same signs in many living things?
questions.answer: Their maker must be one and the same Creator.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the apple with the inhabitants of the world?
questions.answer: It treats them as belonging to one shared created family under the same Lord.

questions.question: Why does the argument move from the apple to the entire earth?
questions.answer: Because understanding the fruit correctly requires seeing the larger setting in which it is produced.

questions.question: What is meant by saying the cosmos is like the apple’s factory?
questions.answer: The whole universe serves in the processes that lead to the fruit’s formation.

questions.question: What does the image of a book suggest when speaking about the universe?
questions.answer: It suggests that creation carries meaning and points back to its author.

questions.question: How does every fruit function in relation to that “book”?
questions.answer: Each fruit is like a sign that helps identify the one who wrote and arranged it.

questions.question: What final belief does the passage invite the reader to accept?
questions.answer: That all provision and creation point clearly to the unity of Allah.

questions.question: In the passage, what does a single apple prove besides being food?
questions.answer: It proves that its existence and delivery come from a Creator with control over the whole universe.

questions.question: Why is the fruit linked with night, day, and the seasons?
questions.answer: Because those repeated changes are part of the system necessary for the fruit to appear.

questions.question: What does the ship comparison teach about the earth?
questions.answer: It teaches that the earth is carrying provisions to living beings in an ordered way.

questions.question: Who benefits from this carrying of provision?
questions.answer: The needy creatures living on earth, especially human beings.

questions.question: What do the visible qualities of the apple reveal according to the passage?
questions.answer: They reveal planned making, mercy, and a connection to Divine wisdom.

questions.question: How is the same message repeated beyond one apple?
questions.answer: The same signs are said to appear in all similar fruits and throughout living creation.

questions.question: Why does this repeated pattern matter for understanding tawhid?
questions.answer: Because one repeated pattern across creation points to one Creator, not many separate powers.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by calling the Creator the sovereign of the apple and the world?
questions.answer: It means the same Lord owns, governs, and creates both the small part and the whole.

questions.question: How do the images of garden, tree, factory, and workshop work together?
questions.answer: They show that the apple belongs to a broad, interconnected process prepared for its growth.

questions.question: What is the importance of saying every fruit is a seal?
questions.answer: A seal identifies its owner, so every fruit identifies the One who made it.

questions.question: How does the number of fruits affect the force of the proof?
questions.answer: The more fruits there are, the more often the proof of Divine unity is displayed.

questions.question: Give a one-sentence summary of the passage.
questions.answer: One fruit is enough to show that the Creator of that fruit is also the Creator of the earth and the whole universe.

questions.question: What example does the passage use to discuss provision and creation?
questions.answer: It uses the example of an apple given to a person as sustenance.

questions.question: What does the passage say must be under control for that apple to reach a person?
questions.answer: The changing seasons, the cycle of day and night, and the movement of the earth must be under control.

questions.question: Why is the earth compared to something that transports goods?
questions.answer: To show that it serves as a means by which provisions are brought to living beings.

questions.question: What can we learn from the description of people waiting for fruits?
questions.answer: We learn that people are in need and depend on provision sent by Allah.

questions.question: What inner meaning is attached to the features of the apple?
questions.answer: Its features are treated as signs of wisdom, mercy, and created dependence.

questions.question: How does the passage use comparison between one apple and all other fruits?
questions.answer: It argues that because the same signs appear in all of them, they must come from the same Maker.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the relationship between the small and the large in creation?
questions.answer: A small thing cannot be understood properly apart from the greater system it belongs to.

questions.question: Why is the maker of the apple also said to be the maker of the apple’s “brothers”?
questions.answer: Because related created things share one order, one pattern, and one source.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the apple’s garden teach us about the earth?
questions.answer: It teaches that the earth is a prepared place where the fruit is grown and sustained.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the universe as a book teach us?
questions.answer: It teaches that creation has meaning and points to its author through many signs.

questions.question: In what way is every fruit a witness?
questions.answer: Every fruit bears testimony to the oneness of the Creator by showing His mark.

questions.question: What is the strongest overall inference from the passage?
questions.answer: If one fruit carries the signs of the whole order of creation, then its giver and maker is Allah alone.
